87474974.title: File:Mackerel steaks in tomato onion sauce (2254411745).jpg

ObjectName.value: Mackerel steaks in tomato onion sauce (2254411745)

Categories.value: Mackerel dishes|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Images from Indian Home cooking Flickr group uploaded by Netha Hussain

ImageDescription.value:
My dad's recipe

Clean 8 mackerel steaks and make cuts on the sides of the pieces that are thick. Mix 2 tsp chilli powder + 1 tsp turmeric powder + salt + few drops of water to make a thick paste. Coat the exposed meat of the mackeral with the paste and also push some down the cuts in the fish pieces <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/rovingi/2206581316/">(pic here)</a>. Keep aside.

Grind to a fine paste 2 medium onions + 3 cloves garlic by adding some water. Heat 3 tbsp olive oil in a fry pan. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds + 1 sprig curry leaves + 1" finely chopped ginger fry for 10 seconds. Add the onion paste and fry for 15-20 minutes stirring occassionally until the paste is dry. Add 1 tsp cumin powder + 1tsp garam masala + 1 tbsp corriander powder + 1 tsp chilli powder and mix well. Add 2 chopped tomatoes + 3 chopped green chillies and fry for 15 minutes while stirring until the sauce is well blended. Remove from heat and keep aside.

Add sufficient sunflower oil to a thick bottomed fry pan to fry the fish. Depth of oil should ne ~1cm. Wait until the oil is slightly smoking. Add the fish pieces and fry on both sides until done and crisp on the outside <a href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/rovingi/2205793869/in/photostream/">(pic here)</a>

Place the sauce back on the heat and add 1 cup of water. When the sauce starts to boil, add salt + 1 tbsp kasturi methi (dry fenugreek leaves) + a few squirts of tomato ketchup.. Boil for 5 min while stirring.

Add the fried fish to the sauce and serve with boiled rice.

Credit.value: Mackerel steaks in tomato onion sauce

ImageDescription.value:
Great curry fix! Today's mutton curry was spicy with a nice tang from tomatoes, but the meat could have been cooked a little longer. The beef rendang was rather mild in comparison, but more tender meat. The smoky eggplant masala was rich and silky with a great warmth from a a slightly sweet chilli sambal.

Rich Maha Restaurant (03) 9670 8998 Shop 9 / 343 Little Collins St

Melbourne VIC 3000

ImageDescription.value:
This image showcases a classic South Indian dish served in a contemporary restaurant setting. The main item is a dosa, a savory crepe made from a fermented batter of rice and lentils, which has been partially eaten to reveal its filling.
The meal is authentically presented on a fresh banana leaf placed over a dark wooden platter. It is accompanied by three essential condiments in small white bowls: a tangy sambar (lentil-based vegetable stew), a spicy red tomato chutney, and a fresh white coconut chutney garnished with black mustard seeds. The background shows a typical restaurant table setting, including a glass of water and a promotional menu.

Categories.value: Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from rice tag of Alpha Flickr stream uploaded by Netha Hussain

ImageDescription.value:
Fried Fish, Lamb Curry, French Beans with Basmatic Rice - Tastes of Singapore 2 meat and 1 veg rice special AUD6.50

Good lamb curry and crispy fried fish. I love the turmeric and other spices used to marinate fried fish!

--- Feeling the need for some Malaysian spice. Not Indian, not Korean, not Japanese. So we decided to give Tastes of Singapore a go. We had heard that they do a decent satay.

The food is definitely very typical of a <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamak_stall">Mamak stall</a> in Singapore or Malaysia.

We didn't have any (lamb or chicken) satays this time, but they looked and smelled quite good, and were done on the grill!

They even have tables outside, and when it is 36°C in the shade, really makes it feel like a Mamak stall in Malaysia!

Best of all, the food is very reasonably priced!


Taste Of Singapore 162 Clayton Rd Clayton 3168 (03) 9544 7865

It is a common liking to top the chana dal chutney with fried curry leaves, fried crisp urad dal, etc which add an additional layer of taste. ImageDescription.value: Aloo Tikki is a popular street food in North India, made of boiled potatoes, peas, and various curry spices. "Alu" means potato, and "tikki" means a small cutlet or croquette in Hindi-Urdu and Marathi. It is served hot along with a side of saunth, tamarind, and coriander-mint sauce, and sometimes dahi (yogurt) or chickpeas.

Watch Aloo Tikki Recipe video in Hindi by Sonia Goyal.

The mixture of boiled and mashed potatoes with some Indian spices is formed into the shape of patty and shallow fried with oil!

Aloo tikki recipe is most famous snack recipe from North Indian cuisine and a popular street food too. Aloo tikki is associated with many recipes like : aloo tikki chola chaat, burger, aloo tikki dahi chaat etc. It is one of the most easiest and quick snacks recipe which can be prepared in jiffy and usually served with green or tamarind chutney, and with chola or with yogurt using raw vegetables and spices.

ImageDescription.value: Vada Pav, alternatively spelt Vada Pao, Wada Pav, or Wada Pao, is a vegetarian fast food dish native to the Indian state of Maharashtra. The dish consists of a deep fried potato dumpling placed inside a bread bun (pav) sliced almost in half through the middle. It is generally accompanied with one or more chutneys and a green chilli pepper.[1] It originated as cheap street food in Mumbai, but is now served in food stalls and restaurants across India.

Panipuri originated from the Magadha region of India. The English meaning of golgappa is "watery bread" or "crisp sphere eaten." The literal meaning suggests that it may have originated from Varanasi. 
It consists of a round, hollow puri, fried crisp and filled with a mixture of flavored water, tamarind chutney, chili, chaat masala, potato, onion and chickpeas.

ImageDescription.value: The Dahi paani-puri is an Indian street food. It consists of hollow crunchy spheres made by frying semolina dough cut outs called "puri". The puri is cracked at the top making a hole. Mashed potatoes are inserted through the hole followed by "dahi" (in hindi dahi means yogurt). At this stage it is called "sukhi puri" (in hindi sukhi means dry). Adding black salted chickpea to the puri is optional. The rest of the puri is now filled with either sweet tamarind water or spicy green chilli and mint water. When the puri breaks in the mouth the flavors of smooth potatoes, spicy water and crunchy puri can be savoured all at once.

ImageDescription.value: Gajar ka halwa; is a carrot-based sweet dessert pudding originally from Punjab; but now it is served all over India and worldwide; it is made mostly in winters by using grated carrots, specific amount of water, milk and sugar, cardamom and dry fruits

Categories.value: Taken with Sony DSC-P150|Gajar ka halwa|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|Homemade foods|Cardamom-based food

ImageDescription.value:
Heat 4 tbsp butter / ghee in a thick bottomed vessel. Add 500 gm grated carrots and fry for 2-3 min while stirring, Add 1 litre whole milk and 15 tsp sugar. Bring to a boil. Add 1tsp crushed cardamom seeds (remove them from the pod). Cook on low heat for 2hrs until the milk evaporates. Garnish with cashew nuts and rasins.

Goes well with Vanilla ice cream

Categories.value: Taken with Canon EOS 50D|Cuisine of New Mexico|Flickr images reviewed by File Upload Bot (Magnus Manske)|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Mango milkshakes|Sparky's Burgers

ImageDescription.value:
One of the most delicious-sounding things at Sparkys is their chili-mango milkshake. If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is.

As far as I can tell, it's mango-flavored soft serve (I think made with vanilla soft serve blended with mango-flavored syrup?), chili powder, topped with whipped cream.

All in all great, but disappointing—the chili part had me thinking they're be a kick, but alas there was none.
